articles.title: Rick, morto em acidente, compôs hino municipal com cantor Daniel | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor e compositor sertanejo, que morreu em acidente em Santa Catarina, ajudou a escrever obra que se tornou símbolo da identidade de Brotas (SP).
articles.summary: Cantor e compositor sertanejo, que morreu em acidente em Santa Catarina, ajudou a escrever obra que se tornou símbolo da identidade de Brotas (SP).
articles.body:
O cantor e compositor Rick , que morreu na queda de um helicóptero em Santa Catarina , deixou uma marca que vai além da música sertaneja. Ao lado do cantor Daniel, ele é coautor do Hino Municipal de Brotas (SP). (Veja hino abaixo)

A obra, que reúne referências à história, à cultura e às paisagens da cidade, se tornou parte da identidade do município.

A Prefeitura de Brotas publicou uma nota de pesar, declarou luto oficial e enalteceu a contribuição artística do cantor para a cidade.

O hino foi oficializado pela Lei Municipal nº 2.262, de 27 de dezembro de 2008 e foi apresentado por Daniel em inauguração de uma escola de Brotas.

Daniel homenageou Rick, de quem era amigo há 32 anos, se solidarizou com familiares e Renner e lembrou dos momentos que viveram juntos. Ele ainda lamentou não terem feito um projeto musical juntos. (Veja abaixo)

Rick, Renner e Daniel no programa 'Viver Sertanejo', da TV Globo, em 2025 — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O hino registrado em 2008, foi apresentado pelo cantor Daniel durante a inauguração da Escola Municipal Professora Edna Soares de Moura Barreto. Desde então, a composição passou a integrar a identidade de Brotas, sendo cantada em escolas e eventos públicos.

'Qual uma bandeira hasteada em verdes campos. Que ventos fazem tremular as gerações. És o cartão postal de tua gente simples. Onde se pode ver e ouvir os corações. Terra encantada hoje cantada em tantos versos. Mãe dedicada que quer ter seus filhos perto. Berço de homens grandes nomes culturais (....)

(...)Brotas querida de minha vida tu és a história. És meu presente futuro a frente. Teu passado é glória. Brotas que cresce, mas não esquece. Quem te faz crescer . Brota paixão no coração de quem te vê'

Lei Municipal de 2008 institui hino de Brotas composto por Rick e Daniel — Foto: Divulgação

O cantor Daniel lamentou a morte do amigo Rick, da dupla Rick e Renner, em uma postagem no Instagram na terça-feira (22).

Rick e outras quatro pessoas morreram na queda de um helicóptero foram, em Urubici, na Serra de Santa Catarina, na segunda (21). Aeronaves dos bombeiros e da Polícia Militar (PM) ajudaram no resgate dos corpos nesta terça.

Além de Rick, morreram o empresário Bruno Avelar; o videomaker Paulo Soares; o piloto Antônio Roberto Nóbrega de Araújo; e o copiloto Leopoldo Barros Teixeira.

O músico de Brotas (SP), que é padrinho da primeira filha de Rick, se despediu do amigo com um texto emocionado. Daniel também perdeu João Paulo, com quem fazia dupla, em um acidente de carro em 1997, em Franco da Rocha.

Cantor Daniel, de Brotas (SP), postou foto de último abraço com o cantor Rick, da dupla Rick e Renner. Eles eram amigos e Daniel é padrinho da filha de Rick — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram e Reprodução/TV Globo

Composições de Rick marcaram a carreira de Daniel

A dupla João Paulo e Daniel foi uma das primeiras parcerias de Rick como compositor, tendo gravado diversas canções suas, entre elas "Poeira da Estrada", "Só Dá Você na Minha Vida", "O Cheiro Dela" e "Olhos Claros".

Em 2025, Daniel recebeu Rick e Renner no programa “Viver Sertanejo”, da TV Globo, e relembrou o início da dupla, como eles inovaram ao trazer a “terceira voz” nas músicas e elogiou o trabalho de Rick como compositor.

Além de dar voz às obras de Rick, Daniel se tornou padrinho da primeira filha do artista, Mônica. Nascida em 1985, ela é a inspiração por trás da faixa “Filha”, que criou como presente para o seu aniversário de 15 anos.

Rick tinha quase 30 anos de casamento com Geralda quando eles decidiram realizar a cerimônia religiosa, em 2015, no Santuário Nacional de Aparecida, no interior de São Paulo. Daniel foi padrinho do artista.

A última vez que cantaram juntos em público foi em fevereiro de 2025, durante a participação de Rick e Renner no “Viver Sertanejo”. No programa, apresentado por Daniel, o trio cantou “Página de Amigos”, escrita por Rick e gravada por Chitãozinho e Xororó em 1995.

Rick, Renner e Daniel no programa 'Viver Sertanejo' da TV Globo, em 2025 — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Os destroços do helicóptero que transportava o cantor Rick, da dupla Rick e Renner, foram localizados na terça-feira (22) em uma área de difícil acesso na região de Santa Bárbara, em Urubici (SC).

A aeronave havia desaparecido na segunda-feira (21) durante um voo entre Porto Belo e São Joaquim. Após uma grande operação de buscas, envolvendo bombeiros, cães farejadores, drones e aeronaves, os destroços foram encontrados em uma área de montanhas e mata fechada.

Devido ao difícil acesso ao local, a retirada dos corpos foi realizada por via aérea com o auxílio de cordas. As vítimas foram encaminhadas ao Instituto Médico Legal (IML) de Florianópolis para exames periciais.

O helicóptero, um Bell 430 fabricado em 2001, estava com a documentação e a certificação de operação regularizadas junto à Anac. Registros indicavam presença de nevoeiro na região no momento das buscas.

Gif mostra infográfico sobre queda de helicóptero onde estava o cantor Rick — Foto: Arte/g1

'A Prefeitura de Brotas manifesta profundo pesar pelo falecimento de Geraldo Antônio de Carvalho, o cantor e compositor Rick e se solidariza com familiares e amigos das demais vítimas do acidente ocorrido em Santa Catarina.

Em respeito à sua memória e à contribuição deixada para a história de Brotas, o município decretou luto oficial.

Com uma trajetória de décadas dedicada à música sertaneja, Rick construiu uma carreira reconhecida como cantor, compositor e produtor, deixando sua marca na música brasileira e no gênero sertanejo.

Para Brotas, sua trajetória ganha um significado ainda mais especial. Ao lado do cantor Daniel, Rick é autor do Hino Municipal de Brotas, obra que reúne em seus versos elementos da história, da cultura, da natureza e da identidade de nossa cidade.

O hino tornou-se parte da memória coletiva dos brotenses e permanece como um legado artístico que atravessa gerações. Por meio dele, a obra de Rick seguirá presente na vida de Brotas, cantada por sua gente e integrada à história do município.

Neste momento de despedida, a Prefeitura de Brotas se solidariza com familiares, amigos, colegas de profissão e admiradores de Rick, desejando conforto e serenidade a todos que sentem sua partida.

Brotas se despede de um artista cuja obra permanecerá entre nós e que deixou seu nome registrado na história de nossa cidade.'

articles.title: Total de pessoas com ensino superior mais que dobrou no PI em 13 anos entre a população ocupada; taxa ainda é a 6ª menor | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados foram divulgados nesta quarta (23) pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) por meio da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua (PNAD Contínua), sobre as características adicionais do mercado de trabalho do país em 2025.
articles.summary: Dados foram divulgados nesta quarta (23) pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) por meio da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua (PNAD Contínua), sobre as características adicionais do mercado de trabalho do país em 2025.
articles.body:
Número de pessoas com ensino superior mais que dobrou no Piauí em 13 anos entre a população ocupada — Foto: Divulgação/Senai-MA

A proporção de pessoas ocupadas no Piauí que têm o ensino superior completo mais que dobrou no período entre 2012 e 2025 , conforme a Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua (PNAD Contínua). Os dados foram divulgados nesta quarta (23) pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

As informações tratam das características adicionais do mercado de trabalho do país em 2025. No Piauí, a proporção de pessoas ocupadas com ensino superior era de 9,2% em 2012 e passou para 21,7% em 2025 .

Mesmo com essa melhoria no nível de ensino dos trabalhadores piauienses no mercado de trabalho, o estado ainda ocupa a sexta menor classificação entre todas as unidades da federação.

No Brasil, essa proporção saiu de 14,1% para 24,9% no mesmo período. As unidades da federação com os maiores indicadores em 2025 são: Distrito Federal (45,9%), São Paulo (30,0%) e Rio de Janeiro (29,1%). Os menores indicadores, por sua vez, ficaram com: Pará (14,1%), Maranhão (16,4%) e Bahia (18,0%).

Quanto ao total de trabalhadores ocupados, que tinham pelo menos o ensino médio , em 2012, havia um total de 35,8% no Piauí. No ano de 2025 essa proporção saltou para 61%, um incremento de 25,2 pontos percentuais no período.

No país, a taxa foi de 68,5%. Entre as unidades da federação, as maiores proporções ficaram com: Distrito Federal (82,4%), São Paulo (76,0%) e Roraima (75,1%). As menores proporções ficaram com: Pará (55,2%), Paraíba (58,4%) e Maranhão (59,6%).

Em 2025, havia cerca de 1,32 milhão de pessoas ocupadas no mercado de trabalho piauiense, e 380 mil delas trabalhavam por conta própria no Piauí (28,7%), sendo que destas um total de 46 mil possuía registro junto ao Cadastro Nacional de Pessoa Jurídica (CNPJ) o que representava 12,2% do total de pessoas que trabalhavam por conta própria no estado, proporção três vezes maior que a registrada em 2012, quando chegava a 4,6%.

Apesar da melhoria na formalização do trabalho com o registro no CNPJ, a proporção de trabalhadores por conta própria com o devido registro ainda era a segunda menor da região Nordeste e a sexta menor do país . No Piauí, do total de cerca de 46 mil pessoas ocupadas por conta própria com registro no CNPJ, 27 mil eram homens (59%) e 19 mil, mulheres (41%).

O registro de pessoas que trabalham por conta própria no CNPJ (geralmente como MEI - Microempreendedor Individual) é altamente positivo para o trabalhador, pois formaliza sua atividade econômica, garante direitos previdenciários e melhora as condições para o crescimento financeiro.

articles.title: Pane no GPS afeta aviões da Embraer fabricados em São José dos Campos | G1
articles.standfirst: Falha afetou a operação de aeronaves da família E2 nesta terça-feira (22) e quarta-feira (23); Azul tem 50 jatos E195-E2 na frota.
articles.summary: A pane no GPS afetou aeronaves Embraer E2 da Azul, provocando atrasos e cancelamentos de voos enquanto a fabricante presta suporte técnico às empresas.
articles.body:
Aviões fabricados pela Embraer em São José dos Campos , no interior de São Paulo, estão entre as aeronaves afetadas por uma instabilidade global no sistema de GPS . A ocorrência envolve modelos da família E2, incluindo o E195-E2 usado pela Azul.

A falha levou a Azul a anunciar ajustes na operação nesta terça-feira (22) e quarta-feira (23) . Segundo a empresa, o problema no GPS gerou o cancelamento de 80 voos e afeta 8 mil passageiros - saiba mais clicando aqui . A companhia tem atualmente 50 aeronaves E195-E2 na frota e orientou os passageiros a consultar a situação dos voos antes de sair de casa.

A fábrica da Embraer em São José dos Campos abriga a linha de montagem dos jatos comerciais da família E2.

O E195-E2 é o maior modelo da família E2 e o maior jato comercial da Embraer atualmente em produção. Dependendo da configuração escolhida pela companhia aérea, o avião transporta até 146 passageiros e foi desenvolvido principalmente para rotas de média densidade e alta frequência.

Segundo a Embraer, o modelo conta com novas asas, motores de última geração e sistemas de voo atualizados em relação à geração anterior dos E-Jets, com foco em eficiência operacional.

Azul celebrou no início de setembro a chegada de mais um modelo E195-E2 da Embraer, o 50º em operação pela companhia — Foto: Guilherme Ramos

A relação entre a Azul e o E195-E2 começou ainda no início da operação comercial do modelo. A companhia foi a primeira aérea do mundo a receber a aeronave, em 2019 , e chegou à marca de 50 unidades na frota em setembro deste ano.

Também em setembro, a Embraer celebrou a entrega do 2.000º E-Jet produzido pela empresa. A aeronave era justamente um E195-E2 destinado à Azul.

A instabilidade no GPS que afeta parte da frota E2 ocorre em um momento de forte demanda pelos aviões da Embraer. No segundo trimestre deste ano, a fabricante entregou 65 aeronaves e registrou receita recorde de R$ 11,3 bilhões.

No primeiro semestre, foram 109 aviões entregues, cerca de 20% a mais que no mesmo período de 2025. A carteira de pedidos também atingiu o recorde de US$ 34,5 bilhões no trimestre, o sétimo consecutivo da empresa.

Azul faz operação do E195-E2 — Foto: Luíza Veneziani/g1

Segundo a Embraer, a empresa recebeu relatos de instabilidade no sistema de GPS que afeta alguns tipos de aeronaves, entre eles os E2. A fabricante informou que acompanha a situação junto aos operadores e ao fabricante do equipamento e presta suporte técnico às companhias.

A instabilidade no GPS provocou cancelamentos e atrasos em voos da Azul em diferentes aeroportos do país. Em Viracopos, em Campinas, principal hub da Azul, voos foram cancelados nesta terça-feira (22). No estado de Minas Gerais, voos no Aeroporto Internacional de Belo Horizonte, em Confins, também foram cancelados.

A Embraer afirmou que os aviões da família E2 possuem sistemas e procedimentos de navegação que permitem a operação mesmo em condições de instabilidade no GPS. Segundo a fabricante, não há impacto na segurança de voo.

A Anac informou que monitora a situação junto à fabricante e aos operadores das aeronaves. A agência também orienta que passageiros afetados por alterações nos voos recebam as informações e a assistência previstas nas regras do transporte aéreo.

A Azul informou que, por precaução, está adotando medidas operacionais que podem resultar em ajustes na malha e nos horários de alguns voos. A companhia orienta os passageiros a consultar o status da reserva antes de seguir para o aeroporto.

“A Embraer foi notificada sobre relatos de instabilidade no sistema GPS que afeta alguns tipos de aeronaves, entre elas o E2, e acompanha a situação de perto junto aos operadores e ao fabricante do equipamento.

A empresa está fornecendo suporte técnico aos clientes e conduzindo as ações necessárias para a resolução da questão. Embora a ocorrência possa afetar a programação operacional de companhias aéreas, não há impacto na segurança de voo.

A frota global de aeronaves E2 dispõe de sistemas e procedimentos de navegação para operar mesmo em condições de instabilidade no sistema GPS, capazes de garantir uma operação segura em conformidade com os requisitos aplicáveis das autoridades de aviação civil.”

"A Azul informa que uma instabilidade global no sistema de GPS impactou a operação de aeronaves Embraer E2-195 e levou ao cancelamento de mais de 80 voos ao longo do dia de ontem. Em consequência dos cancelamentos, alguns voos também sofreram atrasos, com impacto para mais de 8 mil Clientes.

A Azul reforça que os Clientes afetados estão recebendo a assistência prevista na Resolução 400 da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) e que as medidas operacionais foram adotadas com foco na segurança, valor primordial para a Companhia."

articles.title: Versão pagode de 'Ela é Demais' apresentou hit para novas gerações | G1
articles.standfirst: Releitura feita por cantor gaúcho se espalhou por festas e carnavais e ajudou a apresentar a música a novas gerações.
articles.summary: Releitura feita por cantor gaúcho se espalhou por festas e carnavais e ajudou a apresentar a música a novas gerações.
articles.body:
Lançada por Rick & Renner em 1998, "Ela É Demais" ultrapassou as fronteiras do sertanejo nos anos 2000 ao ser adaptada para o pagode por um cantor gaúcho . A releitura se espalhou por festas e carnavais e ajudou a apresentar a música a novas gerações .

Com a morte de Rick , confirmada nesta terça-feira (22) após acidente de helicóptero, o pagodeiro conhecido como Zico Possolino relembrou a história por trás da nova versão e o apoio que recebeu do sertanejo. Segundo ele, o artista autorizou a versão e acompanhou de perto o sucesso da adaptação .

"Rick me abraçou em 2003 ou 2004 e me autorizou a cantar a música. De certo modo, fui apadrinhado", conta.

Segundo Zico, o encontro aconteceu depois que a versão gaúcha de "Ela É Demais" já havia conquistado espaço em festas e carnavais. O pagodeiro gravou a música em 2001 em um bar na Zona Sul de Porto Alegre e viu a canção explodir durante apresentações no Carnaval de Cidreira, no Litoral Norte do Rio Grande do Sul.

Na época, de acordo com Zico, a dupla teria ficado surpresa ao descobrir que uma banda de pagode do RS havia transformado o sucesso sertanejo em um fenômeno de outro gênero musical.

"Eles sabiam que existia uma banda em Porto Alegre que tinha levado 'Ela É Demais' mais para frente. Disseram do orgulho que tinham de saber que saiu aqui do Rio Grande do Sul. Eles não imaginavam, porque é um estado muito voltado ao tradicionalismo", lembra.

Passados 25 anos da gravação, Zico afirma que a versão pagodeira continua sendo presença constante em festas pelo país e até no exterior. Segundo ele, DJs costumam recorrer à música para animar pistas de dança e vídeos da canção já chegaram de países como Canadá, Japão e Portugal.

O cantor gaúcho ainda relembrou com gratidão o incentivo que recebeu de Rick ao longo da trajetória de "Ela É Demais".

"Tenho poucos ídolos na minha vida. Rick é um deles", diz.

Como 'Ela É Demais', sucesso de Rick & Renner, ganhou o Brasil em versão de pagode — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Jovem com tipo raro de leucemia busca ajuda para conseguir medicamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Ítalo Peixoto descobriu a doença em fevereiro e já passou por tratamentos disponíveis na rede pública; medicamento importado é necessário para que ele possa entrar em remissão e fazer transplante de medula.
articles.summary: Ítalo Peixoto descobriu a doença em fevereiro e já passou por tratamentos disponíveis na rede pública.
articles.body:
Um jovem de Montes Claros , no Norte de Minas, busca ajuda para conseguir um medicamento necessário para o tratamento de um tipo raro de leucemia. Ítalo Peixoto, que descobriu a doença em fevereiro deste ano, precisa de um remédio importado que custa cerca de R$ 800 mil. (No vídeo acima, veja a reportagem completa sobre a luta de Ítalo contra a doença).

Ítalo foi diagnosticado com leucemia linfoblástica aguda de células T, um tipo raro de câncer no sangue.

“[Na época], eu pesquisei no Google e sempre falava que era dengue, não falava que era câncer. Na minha cabeça, nunca pensei que passaria por isso. Entrei em pânico, fiquei angustiado”, relembra como foi a descoberta da doença.

Ítalo foi diagnosticado com leucemia linfoblástica aguda de células T — Foto: Reprodução/Inter 1

Desde então, a rotina de Ítalo e da esposa, Júlia, passou a ser dividida entre hospitais, exames e tratamentos. Segundo a família, ele já passou por todas as opções de tratamento disponíveis na rede pública, mas a doença continua avançando.

“Ela [a doença] é uma multiplicação de células cancerígenas imaturas dentro da medula óssea, que é a fábrica do sangue. Então, a fábrica do sangue vai sendo substituída por doença, vai ocupando não só a medula óssea, mas vai ocupando o sistema nervoso central, as ínguas, que são os linfonodos, o fígado, o baço e, infelizmente, se não tratada, é fatal”, explicou a médica que o acompanha, Isabela Câmara.

Segundo a médica, Ítalo precisa de um transplante de medula óssea. Antes, porém, é necessário que a doença entre em remissão, ou seja, fique controlada. Para isso, o jovem precisa utilizar a nelarabina, medicamento importado que, segundo a família, custa cerca de R$ 800 mil.

“Ela é menos disponível, uma medicação importada, e tem a vantagem de atuar especificamente contra os linfócitos T. Uma medicação eficaz e estudada neste tipo de leucemia”.

Diante do alto custo, familiares e amigos começaram uma mobilização para arrecadar o dinheiro necessário para a compra do medicamento. Até o momento, cerca de 10% do valor já havia sido arrecadado.

Apesar das dificuldades, uma notícia trouxe esperança à família: a irmã de Ítalo, Paloma Peixoto, é 100% compatível para o transplante de medula.

“Fiquei muito feliz, me senti muito abençoada, eu fiquei muito emocionada porque a gente sabe que é difícil encontrar um doador, mas graças a Deus encontrou tão perto. Eu estou pronta e disposta para fazer o transplante”, disse Paloma.

O procedimento, no entanto, só poderá ser realizado depois que Ítalo estiver em condições clínicas e a doença estiver controlada. A família mantém a esperança de conseguir o medicamento e seguir com o tratamento.

“Eu tenho uma tatuagem escrito fé, sou muito católico. Nós rezamos todos os dias e creio que Deus vai fazer um milagre na minha vida”, disse Ítalo.

“Nós, seres humanos, temos muito aquilo de correr atrás do material e esquecemos de viver a vida. Hoje, o que a gente mais quer é ter mais uma chance para realmente viver e não só sobreviver”, falou a esposa, Júlia Peixoto.

O dia 18 de julho marcou uma nova etapa para o Terras de Verano , empreendimento da virtú Incorporação e Urbanismo em parceria com a Perplan Urbanismo em Ribeirão Preto.

A abertura oficial de vendas foi realizada no Stand da Perplan Urbanismo, localizado na Av. Giuseppe Cilento , 1881 , e contou com a presença de imobiliárias parceiras, que acompanharam de perto o início da comercialização do projeto.

Depois de um período de expectativa e apresentação do empreendimento ao mercado imobiliário, o encontro representou o momento de transformar o interesse construído durante o pré-lançamento em uma nova fase do Terras de Verano.

Antes da abertura oficial, o Terras de Verano já vinha sendo apresentado ao mercado por meio de ações voltadas a imobiliárias, corretores e potenciais compradores.

No dia 18 de julho, parceiros comerciais se reuniram no Stand da Perplan Urbanismo para acompanhar o início das vendas e conhecer ainda mais de perto a proposta do empreendimento.

“A abertura de vendas está acontecendo aqui no Stand da Perplan Urbanismo. Nós acreditamos no projeto desde que ele nasceu e, hoje, comprovamos o sucesso absoluto que esse projeto está sendo no mercado”, disse Edna Gasparini, imobiliária parceira.

Com a abertura das vendas, o projeto deu início a uma nova fase de sua trajetória. O evento no Stand da Perplan Urbanismo marcou mais um passo na chegada do Terras de Verano ao mercado de Ribeirão Preto.

Um projeto criado para quem busca espaço para crescer, compartilhar momentos, construir memórias e criar raízes. Mais do que morar, viver com propósito. Isso é viver Verano.

articles.title: Rio registra setembro mais chuvoso em 29 anos, segundo Alerta Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Capital fluminense já acumula 163,2 mm de chuva e supera o recorde anterior, registrado em 2005, segundo o Sistema Alerta Rio.
articles.summary: A cidade do Rio de Janeiro registrou o mês de setembro mais chuvoso dos últimos 29 anos antes mesmo do fim do período. O recorde foi alcançado nesta quarta-feira (23).
articles.body:
Rio de Janeiro registra chuva nesta quarta-feira (23) — Foto: Adilson Coutinho/ TV Globo

A cidade do Rio de Janeiro registrou o mês de setembro mais chuvoso dos últimos 29 anos antes mesmo do fim do período. O recorde foi alcançado nesta quarta-feira (23), de acordo com o Sistema Alerta Rio, serviço meteorológico da Prefeitura do Rio.

Até as 8h45, a capital fluminense havia acumulado 163,2 mm de chuva ao longo do mês. O volume supera os 157,7 mm registrados em setembro de 2005, que, até então, era o maior índice desde o início da série histórica do Alerta Rio.

O terceiro maior acumulado para setembro foi registrado em 2022, quando choveu 144,7 mm.

Em quase todas as regiões da cidade, o volume de chuva já ultrapassou os 100 mm. Em alguns pontos, o acumulado supera o dobro da média climatológica para o mês.

Rio registra setembro mais chuvoso dos últimos 29 anos — Foto: Dhara Pereira/ Arte g1

O cenário é explicado pela passagem de sucessivas frentes frias pela costa da Região Sudeste desde o início de setembro. O fenômeno favoreceu a ocorrência de chuva e a entrada de ar frio no estado do Rio de Janeiro.

Além disso, a circulação de ventos em diferentes níveis da atmosfera contribui para manter a umidade elevada, favorecendo a formação de áreas de instabilidade.

Segundo a meteorologista Hana Silveira, da Climatempo, o El Niño tem participação nesse cenário, mas não é o único fator responsável pelo aumento das chuvas.

“O El Niño tem um papel importante neste cenário. É um fenômeno climático relevante que alterou o regime de chuvas em várias regiões do país, mas não explica sozinho essa situação. Outro fenômeno muito importante é a Oscilação Antártica, uma variação nos campos de pressão e nos ventos que ocorre ao redor do continente antártico”, afirmou.

Painel eletrônico recomenda cautela aos motoristas no Jardim Botânico, na Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: Charles Mathura/ TV Globo

De acordo com a especialista, a Oscilação Antártica influenciou principalmente a primeira quinzena do mês, favorecendo períodos de instabilidade e dias chuvosos no estado.

“Esse fenômeno tem fases positiva e negativa. Na fase positiva, as massas de ar frio encontram mais dificuldade para avançar em direção ao Brasil. Já na fase negativa, ocorre o contrário: a chegada de massas de ar frio e de frentes frias é favorecida”, explicou.

A passagem de uma nova frente fria continua influenciando o tempo no Rio neste primeiro dia da primavera. Nesta quarta-feira (23), o céu permanece encoberto, com previsão de chuva ao longo de todo o dia.

Na quinta-feira (24), o céu deve seguir nublado, com chuva de fraca a moderada intensidade e acumulados menores do que os registrados nesta quarta.

Já na sexta-feira (25), o tempo continuará predominantemente nublado, mas o sol poderá aparecer entre muitas nuvens durante a tarde. A chuva perde intensidade e tende a ocorrer de forma isolada, com volumes reduzidos. As temperaturas voltam a subir, e a máxima prevista para a capital é de 27°C.

articles.title: At least 11 people killed in South Africa township shooting
articles.summary: Armed men open fire at a house party in a Durban township, killing a pregnant woman and 10 others.
articles.body:
At least 11 people, including a pregnant woman, have been killed after armed men stormed a house in a township in the South African city of Durban.

The attack took place late on Tuesday, according to Thamsanqa Ntuli, the premier of KwaZulu-Natal province, of which Durban is the main city. Assailants entered the home shortly before 11pm (21:00 GMT) while the victims were gathered at a house party.

Two people survived the attack, Ntuli said, adding the motive behind the killings was not immediately clear.

“The incident has left the community in profound shock and grief,” he said.

Local broadcaster eNCA reported that the attackers forced everyone into a single room before opening fire. They also set fire to a car belonging to one of the victims.

“It’s shocking and sad. These are guys I grew up with. I can’t believe it. It’s like a movie,” a resident told the broadcaster.

“I’ve been staying here all my life, and I’ve never seen anything like this,” he added.

According to a police statement cited by eNCA, preliminary investigations indicated that some of those killed were on South Africa’s Crime Intelligence radar over suspected illegal activities, though the statement did not elaborate further.

“Although the motive for the shooting has not yet been confirmed, a feud between rival groupings cannot be ruled out,” the police said.

South Africa has one of the world’s highest murder rates, with an average of about 60 people killed daily in a population of roughly 62 million.

In March, soldiers were deployed alongside national police to violent hotspots to tackle rampant crime, an issue President Cyril Ramaphosa has described as one of the country’s biggest threats.

articles.title: 'This is treason': Rahul Gandhi revives 'vote chori' charge after report of rift within EC
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday revived his \"vote chori\" charge against the Election Commission and accused ele.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday revived his "vote chori" charge against the Election Commission and accused election officials of committing "treason".In a post on X, Rahul said, "I am telling the EC and election officials clearly: What you are doing is wrong. This is treason, this is against the country. Do not forget that. The time will come when we will catch you. You will not be able to escape."His remarks came after an Indian Express report claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections to the poll panel's actions at least 14 times over the past 10 months during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The report said the commissioners had flagged issues relating to the addition and deletion of voters as well as the handling of voter data.Senior Congress leaders KC Venugopal and P Chidambaram also stepped up their attack on the poll panel following the report.Chidambaram said the opposition had already contended that several decisions concerning the SIR were wrong and questioned how Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's view could become the decision of the Commission if the two Election Commissioners had taken a contrary position."The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that if the decision-making process is flawed or wrong, the decision will also be flawed or wrong. The opposition has contended that many decisions concerning SIR were wrong. Now, it is revealed that the decision-making process was also wrong," Chidambaram said."If two ECs have taken a contrary view, how could the CEC make his view the 'decision' of the ECI? All decisions of the ECI in recent years should be reviewed by a Parliamentary Committee. Meanwhile, the SIR process should be suspended immediately all over the country," he added.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal also targeted CEC Gyanesh Kumar and demanded his removal."There is no doubt remaining. Mr Gyanesh Kumar has no right to remain in office. How the hell can one man, acting on His Master's orders, strike off names at whim? How can he sideline fellow Constitutional officers to only take blatantly illegal steps that put our democracy in danger?" Venugopal said."The right to vote is an essential Constitutional power given to every citizen, the fundamental bedrock of our democracy. If it is to be taken away, due process must be followed with utmost probity," he added.EC rejects reports of differencesThe Election Commission, however, rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the SIR and said all decisions related to the exercise were taken unanimously.Officials told news agency PTI that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling, but these did not amount to disagreement with the final decisions taken by the Commission.EC sources said all decisions of the Commission, including those relating to the SIR, had the approval of Sandhu, Joshi and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Officials also pointed out that the law governing the Election Commission, as well as a Supreme Court judgment, provides that decisions should, as far as possible, be taken unanimously. articles.title: UK warned over ballooning debt costs and slower growth ahead of Budget
articles.summary: Higher energy prices due to the conflict in the Middle East and climate change could hit growth.
articles.body:
The UK has been warned over ballooning debt costs and slower economic growth ahead of Chancellor John Healey's first Budget next month.

The UK was among countries facing downgraded growth forecasts in a report by the influential Organisation of Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) on Wednesday.

That came as the head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) told the BBC that Britain and the US needed to reduce debt due to spiralling borrowing costs.

The ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war has pushed up the cost of crude oil leading to higher fuel and energy costs, which in turn has driven up inflation around the world.

The UK economy will grow by slightly less than expected next year, according to the OECD which now expects growth of 1% next year rather than 1.1%.

However, it said the UK had proved more resilient than expected this year, upgrading its forecast for growth 0.9% to 1.1%.

Meanwhile, IMF head Kristalina Georgieva told the BBC on Tuesday that global economic shocks had been "pushing debt levels up like a staircase not to heaven" but that governments had taken "no action to contain that service cost".

"[It's] time to take that action," she said, adding that "courage" was needed by politicians to take the necessary steps.

Inflation has also pushed up the cost of interest on government debt, which alongside an unexpected surge in government borrowing in August has added to the pressure on Healey.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that the UK's high level of borrowing had left it "over-exposed" to global shocks.

However, he said he stood by his point - made a year ago - that Britain should be less "in hock" to investors in the bond markets. At the time, the comments spooked investors due to fears he was calling for spending restraints to be eased.

Burnham has made easing the cost-of-living for households one of his key aims, while the government is under pressure to spend more on defence.

He and Healey face a difficult balancing act, trying to offer more support to households while sticking to Labour's manifesto commitments on tax and the government's self-imposed fiscal rules.

The impact of higher fuel prices next year depends on how long supply disruptions last, and stockpiles of oil and supplies from outside the Gulf states have helped cushion the effects on economies so far, the OECD said.

Risks to the global economy include weaker-than-expected returns on AI investment and climate-change related supply shocks, the OECD said.

Next year, global growth is expected to also be 0.1% lower, with countries affected including Australia, Canada, and the Euro-area.

Weather-related shocks, including from a strong El Nino, could hit farmers and help push up food prices, it added.

In addition, tariffs and export restrictions on trade continue to add to uncertainty, it said. New US tariffs from July as part of the Trump administration's ongoing volatile trade policy have raised its effective tariff rate by 1%.

Chief Secretary to the Treasury Emma Reynolds said: "Despite unprecedented pressures and conflict in both the Middle East and in Europe, the UK economy is showing strong resilience."

She added that the government is "already giving families space to breathe" and "starting the big, long-term changes needed to create good jobs and growth in every postcode".

However, Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said the OECD urges countries to "control spending and improve public sector efficiency".

"Instead, this government is trying to find new ways to tax you whilst having to pay interest rates on their borrowing which are the highest in the G7," he said.

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said that the UK had "so far remained resilient to higher energy prices", but most of that reflected businesses having built up stock and households not putting so much disposable income into savings.

However, this effect would be temporary, with growth more muted next year.

She added that the "drag" on the economy from energy prices would pick up, while as a percentage of the UK's economic output, debt interest payments are forecast to hit levels seen in the mid-1980s.

articles.title: Polo off Mexican coast is among ‘the strongest storms ever’ as Odalys becomes a hurricane
articles.summary: Hurricane Polo has grown into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades, and it was expected to skirt Mexico’s southwestern coast as a Category 5 storm.
articles.body: MEXICO CITY — Polo has grown into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades and was expected to skirt Mexico’s southwestern coast as a major hurricane, while another Pacific system, Odalys, strengthened Wednesday from a tropical storm to a hurricane without threatening land. The U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami has called Polo an “extremely dangerous” storm and forecast the system would turn sharply to the northwest before moving west-northwest over the next several days. Polo was about 165 miles (266 kilometers) south of Zihuatanejo and 320 miles (515 kilometers) southeast of Manzanillo, the center reported. It was moving slowly north with maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (241 kph). That put it at Category 4 strength, after earlier being a Category 5 storm. “Fluctuations in intensity are expected, but Polo is expected to remain a very powerful major hurricane during the next few days,” the NHC said. Odalys was a Category 1 hurricane and was about 1,295 miles (2,085 kilometers) off the southern tip of the Baja California peninsula of Mexico, moving east-northeast at 9 mph (15 kph) with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph (120 kph), the hurricane center said. Waves, flooding and mudslides are all risks Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said experts indicated Polo was not likely to touch land. Still, hurricane-force winds extend up to 40 miles (65 kilometers) from the storm’s center and tropical storm-force winds up to 105 miles (169 kilometers) from the eye, the U.S. center said. Tropical storm conditions were expected along the Pacific coast in Guerrero, Michoacan and Colima states Wednesday into Thursday. Polo on Tuesday became the third Category 5 hurricane of the Pacific season, following Genevieve and Lowell earlier this year. Category 5 is the highest level on the Saffir-Simpson scale, reflecting that a storm has maximum sustained winds exceeding 157 mph (253 kph). The hurricane set residents along Mexico’s Pacific coast on edge once again after being walloped by a number of powerful cyclones in recent years. Beaches emptied and dark clouds swirled above choppy seas, while Mexican authorities temporarily suspended classes Tuesday in a number of areas. Mexico’s navy shut down ports in the states of Guerrero and Michoacán and warned civilians and fishermen to take care. Concepción López Villegas was busily preparing her seaside restaurant for what may come. Strong waves were already lapping at the coastline of her city Lázaro Cárdenas in Michoacán. As men and children watched the stirring waters behind her, López Villegas said she feared powerful waves would destroy the small business she has worked decades to build. “We’re worried and trying to protect our businesses,” López Villegas said. “And of course, we’re sad because it’s our heritage, our legacy that from one moment to another could be destroyed.” U.S. National Hurricane Center data shows Polo’s winds reached speeds comparable to only a few hurricanes in the region in recent decades, primarily Hurricane Patricia, which had winds that reached 215 mph (346 kph) in 2015. “This is one of the strongest storms ever in the (Pacific) Basin,” said Kristen L. Corbosiero, professor at the University at Albany’s Department of Atmospheric & Environmental Sciences. Heavy rain could produce flash flooding and mudslides. About 3 to 6 inches (8 to 15 centimeters) of rain was forecast for Guerrero and Michoacán states, with smaller amounts possible for coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima and Jalisco states. El Nino fueled rapid intensification The U.S. Embassy in Mexico issued a weather alert, instructing citizens to avoid water and beaches and to heed warnings from Mexican authorities. “Even if the storm does not make direct landfall, heavy rain may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides. Hazardous ocean conditions — intensified by storms — may result in deadly rip currents and rogue waves,” the embassy wrote in a statement. The rapid intensification of the storm has stunned scientists and authorities alike, with the NHC writing in a report that it was “truly remarkable” how quickly Polo gained strength in 24 hours. Philip Klotzbach, research scientist in the Department of Atmospheric Science at Colorado State University, attributed the intensification to the weather phenomenon known as El Nino, which has fueled crippling droughts in Mexico and Central America and floods in other parts of the region. In the Pacific, it has resulted in warmer waters and wind patterns that act as fodder for hurricanes, he said. “There are all the ingredients that hurricanes need to get really strong really fast,” Klotzbach said. No Atlantic hurricanes have formed yet this year, and this year has set a record for the longest start to a season without a hurricane. The effects of this year’s El Nino crush storms before they get going.

articles.title: What's Suwalki gap? Europe's 'achilles heel' that it fears could be Putin's target
articles.summary: Europe News: Belarusian tanks rolling close to the Polish and Lithuanian border last week, followed almost immediately by Ukraine's biggest strike deep inside Russ.
articles.body: Belarusian tanks rolling close to the Polish and Lithuanian border last week, followed almost immediately by Ukraine's biggest strike deep inside Russia, has pushed a little known patch of land back into the spotlight.Barely 100 kilometres long, the Suwalki Gap is the only route by land connecting the three Baltic states (Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia) to the rest of Nato. The European leaders and security officials worry it could become the place where Vladimir Putin chooses to test the alliance without firing the first shot of a full scale war.The gap sits squeezed between Belarus on one side and Kaliningrad on the other, a heavily armed Russian territory, which is not part of the mainland Russia.Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave, was once German land and home to a large German population for centuries, until the Soviet Union took it over after the Nazi army collapsed at the end of the World War II.It was then formally handed to Moscow under the Potsdam Agreement of 1945, signed by the wartime allies as they carved up the map of Europe. It has stayed Russian ever since, cut off from the Russian mainland and sitting right between Poland and Lithuania like a loaded gun pointed at Nato's eastern edge.Why the gap is being watched so closelyIf this narrow corridor were ever blocked or seized, the Baltic states would effectively be sealed off from reinforcement by land. Troops, tanks, fuel and ammunition all rely on this single stretch to move from Poland northwards. That is exactly why Nato treats it as a strategic weak spot, even though there is no solid proof right now that Russia plans to attack it.The Belarusian drills involved mechanised and armoured units training in border defence, counter sabotage work and responses to drones. Minsk called them purely defensive and said their scale stayed below the level requiring advance notice under international agreements, but their location so close to the Suwalki Gap still drew immediate attention from Western capitals.The suspicion compounded after Ukraine's deep strike on Russia, which was also the biggest since 2022 when the war began.A test of nerves?There is, however, no public evidence that Moscow is preparing to seize the corridor or launch a direct attack on Nato territory. The concern lies instead in the possibility of pressure below the threshold of open conflict, including drone incursions, sabotage, cyberattacks and military manoeuvres that could test Nato's ability to distinguish between deliberate aggression and incidents that can be denied or attributed elsewhere.Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Nato has strengthened its eastern flank with multinational forces, reinforcement plans and pre-positioned equipment stretching from the Baltic region to southeastern Europe.The measures are intended to ensure that any attempt to disrupt access to the Baltic states can be met quickly and collectively. However, for European security planners, the Suwalki Gap is therefore less a prediction of where the next conflict will begin than a reminder of how it could be its "achilles heel".ALSO READ | Russia planning 'grey zone operations'? articles.title: U.S. warns Australia’s social media algorithm reforms risk ‘facilitating censorship’
articles.summary: The Trump administration has criticized Australia’s proposed social media algorithm reforms, which would give users the option to choose the content on their feeds, warning that Washington would most likely view them as “facilitating censorship.”
articles.body: SYDNEY — The Trump administration has criticized Australia’s proposed social media algorithm reforms, which would give users the option to choose the content on their feeds, warning that Washington would most likely view them as “facilitating censorship.” Under draft laws proposed this month by Australia’s center-left Labor government, social media platforms would be required to notify users and offer a default algorithm-recommended content feed, with the option to opt out and instead see posts only from accounts they choose to follow. In a formal submission to Australia’s public consultation process, the U.S. Embassy in Canberra said late Tuesday that it had “serious concerns” about the proposed law’s goal of mandating how platforms manage content and user feeds. “We are particularly concerned by potential mandates that would allow regulators to impose rigid, one-size-fits-all platform design requirements — such as forced chronological feeds or opt-in recommendation systems,” the statement said. The U.S. warned that the proposed legislation could have implications beyond Australia’s borders, saying the mandated algorithm design requirements “may affect what users see, say and hear not just in or from Australia, but globally.” Washington urged Canberra to clearly define how “harm” and “risk” would be determined, by whom, and against what standard, cautioning that vague definitions risk enabling viewpoint-based censorship by incentivizing platforms to over-moderate protected speech to avoid regulatory penalties. Should Australia compel platforms to aggressively filter algorithmic content in ways that capture protected speech, the U.S. warned, the suppression of a disfavored speaker or media source’s reach would be no different from outright removal. “The U.S. government would likely consider such a measure as facilitating censorship,” the statement said. The comments come as Prime Minister Anthony Albanese attends the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where he has been promoting his government’s technology reform agenda and raising concerns about the risks posed by artificial intelligence. When asked by a reporter about the U.S. criticism of the draft legislation, Albanese said the proposed measure was not intended to grant governments greater authority, but rather to restore individuals’ control over their content choices, which was reflected in the way the policy has been framed. “I will always stand up for Australia’s national interests, and the (reform) is something we have foreshadowed for some time,” Albanese said. The Australian government is seeking feedback from digital platforms, industry bodies, civil society organizations and advocates on the draft “Digital Duty of Care” legislation, with the bill expected to be introduced to parliament this year.

articles.summary: The regulator says it has concerns over how the site is relying on third party checks provided by Apple for some users.
articles.body:
Ofcom has launched an investigation into Pornhub owner, Aylo, over whether the site's new age checks are effectively stopping children from accessing adult content.

The regulator said in May that Pornhub started using a new age verification process for some users, which relied on a third party, Apple.

It said it had concerns that Aylo "may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing" before implementing this new process, and so it "may not be highly effective" at preventing children from seeing pornography.

In a lengthy statement given to the BBC, Aylo strongly defended its system for age verification while stressing it would cooperate fully with the investigation.

Under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA), sites that host pornographic material must use highly effective age assurance to ensure users are over 18, but it leaves it up to the service to decide the method of age-checking it will use.

Ofcom says as part of its investigation it will consider how Aylo implements its age verification processes and whether it conducted the "necessary due diligence" before it was implemented.

It will not investigate how Apple operates its age checks.

George Lusty, Ofcom's Director of Enforcement, said: "Online age checks are a vital protection to prevent children from encountering inappropriate or harmful material, including pornography.

"We expect tech firms to ensure age checks are highly effective before introducing them. Anything less could leave children at risk."

But Aylo argues that, having experimented in multiple markets with multiple age-check methods, Apple's system "provides significantly stronger protection than any other age assurance method currently available in the UK market".

It also notes that Ofcom had previously praised Apple's technology as "a real win for children and families".

Aylo argues a system based on asking individual pornographic sites to check users ages, simply drives users to riskier sites that aren't following Ofcom's rules.

Research by the Lucy Faithfull Foundation has previously suggested that non-compliant sites "may also be more likely to host harmful or illegal content, and in some cases, sexual images of children".

Under the OSA, Ofcom holds the power to fine non-compliant companies up to £18 million or 10% of their annual global turnover, whichever is greater.

This probe is just the latest clash between the regulator and what is one of the world's most viewed porn sites.

In October 2025 Pornhub said traffic from UK users had plunged by more than 75% following the introduction of more robust age checks by the OSA.

Some have questioned whether people were simply using Virtual Private Networks (VPN) to get around the checks instead.

In January, Pornhub announced it would restrict access to its website in the UK, blaming the tougher checks, with only people who had previously made a Pornhub account able to access its content.

Aylo said that updates to the Act requiring age verification had "not achieved its goal of protecting minors".

However, in May, it said it would be making the site available again for some UK Apple users who had confirmed their age with the company's most up-to-date version of iOS, its mobile operating system.

articles.title: Qatar says ‘no alternative to diplomacy’ as Belgium and Rwanda restore ties
articles.summary: Doha lauded for mediating Brussels-Kigali rupture, showcasing its trusted role in international peace efforts.
articles.body:
Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Majed al-Ansari says Doha will keep pushing for diplomacy to end crises around the world from Africa’s Great Lakes region to the Gulf.

Speaking to Al Jazeera on Tuesday, al-Ansari welcomed the restoration of ties between Belgium and Rwanda, 18 months after they expelled each other’s diplomats over the conflict in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

In a joint statement on Tuesday, the two countries thanked Qatar for facilitating their first talks in June 2025, which al-Ansari said led to further diplomatic rapprochement between them.

Al-Ansari said Qatar has long been involved in the Great Lakes region, including mediating between the DRC, Rwanda and the M23 armed group and hosting the June 2025 talks in Doha.

“It was a breakthrough meeting between the two foreign ministers, who hadn’t met for a while, addressing a lot of underlying issues,” he said.

He said Belgium and Rwanda trusted Qatar because of its record of working with both countries.

“This is the way we usually do it. We provide the platform, we provide our trustworthiness, we get the parties involved and then we hope that that trajectory would move in its own right,” he said.

On Tuesday, Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani told the UN General Assembly in New York that as a mediator, Qatar has always sought to resolve disputes through dialogue and negotiations and “reach just and fair solutions grounded in international law”.

Qatar’s foreign minister also met his Iranian counterpart to discuss efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Gulf and create conditions conducive to dialogue.

Al-Ansari told Al Jazeera that there had been some movement in the negotiations to end the United States-Israel war on Iran in recent days despite many setbacks in previous rounds.

“We do believe that there is no alternative to diplomacy, and we cannot afford to let diplomacy fail,” he said.

“Right now, the emphasis is on keeping the lines of communication open, keeping the exchange going and listening to both sides,” he added.

Qatari leaders met US President Donald Trump on Tuesday during the UN General Assembly.

Al-Ansari said they told Trump the effects of the Iran war and of the conflict in Gaza and the occupied West Bank were being felt internationally and would only grow.

He said Qatar was working with Pakistan, Oman and other Gulf Cooperation Council states towards a diplomatic resolution.

“The sooner we get to it, the less the effects will be felt around the world,” he said.

articles.title: What Palestinian children endure in Israeli detention
articles.summary: Every day, Fidaa Zalbani checks the room of her son, Mohammed, 17, tidying his bed and arranging untouched clothes.
articles.body:
Every morning, Fidaa Zalabani checks the room of her 17-year-old son, Mohammed, in the Shu’fat refugee camp in occupied East Jerusalem, arranging clothes that remain untouched by the end of day.

Mohammed hasn’t set foot in his room since Israeli forces arrested him more than three years ago, but his mother repeats the same routine every morning.

He was arrested in February 2023 at the age of 13, accused of stabbing a soldier on a bus at a checkpoint at the Shu’fat refugee camp, two weeks after he saw his teenage friend killed by an Israeli soldier.

During the incident, a security guard opened fire, accidentally shooting the Israeli soldier who had been stabbed, who later died. Mohammed was subsequently sentenced to 18 years in prison, accused of causing the death.

For about two years, Fidaa said she has not been allowed to visit her son at Megiddo Prison in northern Israel, leaving her deeply concerned about his health. She also believes Mohammed and other child detainees have been subjected to beatings and other forms of mistreatment.

“The lawyer told us during several visits that the child detainees there go to sleep hungry most days; the guards allow no more than four loaves of bread for 13 prisoners, a situation that kept me awake worried about his condition,” she told Al Jazeera.

In September 2025, the Israeli Supreme Court found that the Israeli Prison Service has failed to provide Palestinian prisoners with adequate food – although the prison service, which is overseen by far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir – has rejected allegations of starvation.

Fidaa said Megiddo Prison had only recently begun allowing child detainees to bathe more than once a week, a privilege previously denied for more than two years. She said scabies and other skin diseases had spread among detainees amid overcrowding and poor sanitation.

However, Fidaa is most concerned about raids on prison cells, beatings of children, and the practice of tightly restraining them for hours at a time.

Palestinian prisoner advocacy organisations report that, based on available data and documentation, there have been approximately 1,900 arrests of Palestinian children from the occupied West Bank since October 2023, when Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began.

Meanwhile, the number of children detained from the Gaza Strip remains unclear due to ongoing enforced disappearances and the difficulty of accessing information regarding their status.

Palestinian prisoner organisations report that 360 Palestinian children remain detained by Israel. Rights groups and United Nations bodies have documented reports of beatings, severe restrictions on food, medical neglect, solitary confinement, and other forms of ill-treatment of child detainees.

Ola Qatishat, 16, from Tammun in the northern West Bank, was talking to her sister, Asia, at midnight on May 24. She was excitedly discussing plans for a celebration to mark Asia passing her high school exams.

Then the Israeli army raided their home and arrested Ola, accusing her of incitement against Israel. The family have no more details about her charges and remain in shock about her detention.

“We chased after the military vehicle as they hauled her away, screaming, ‘She’s just a child! What are you doing?’ They threw a sound grenade at my mother and me to force us back. Since that day, we have wept over her absence,” Asia told Al Jazeera.

Ola loved school and, shortly before her arrest, had entered a mural-painting competition there. While in detention, she learned from her lawyer that she had won first place across the entire West Bank.

Her sister Asia passed her exams with distinction last July, but, with her sister detained in northern Israel’s Damon Prison, she said she felt no joy.

“The lawyer visited her a month ago and told us she had begun suffering from scabies due to a lack of hygiene and infrequent bathing; an officer stands at the bathroom door, telling each female prisoner, ‘You have five minutes; if you don’t finish bathing, I will come in and drag you out,'” Asia added.

The anxiety of Ola’s family grows daily as she remains in detention, awaiting her court hearing in October.

The conditions raise questions regarding adherence to the special safeguards guaranteed by international law for detained children, particularly as human rights organisations report harsh conditions within Israeli prisons.

Lawyer Lubna Tuma, from the Adalah Legal Center, told Al Jazeera that Palestinian children in Israeli prisons face total isolation from the outside world; when a child is brought to meet their lawyer, they are led in blindfolded, cutting them off from their surroundings and depriving them of sight and a sense of the space around them.

She pointed to an explicit policy of providing only the bare minimum of necessities, explaining that this refers to the minimum required to keep the prisoner alive, rather than what a child needs for growth and the preservation of their health and dignity.

“Under this approach, the Palestinian child is treated as a prisoner to be punished, rather than as a child entitled to specific rights and protections,” she said.

Muin Salahat, 16, from Beit Fajjar, south of Bethlehem, was released last June after spending 16 months in administrative detention, without ever knowing the charges against him.

During his detention, he contracted scabies but received no treatment, a fate shared by other child prisoners in Megiddo Prison. After his release, he developed severe skin lesions, keeping him awake at night.

His father, Ghassan, told Al Jazeera that he persisted in treating his son despite struggling to afford the medication. It took more than two months for Muin’s condition to improve.

Muin does not want to speak to the media, but his father said the effects of his detention remain apparent in his behaviour.

“When we sit down to eat, he leaves his plate untouched and drifts into a trance. Then, he starts talking about the terrible food in prison. Suddenly, he shifts to describing how soldiers would storm the cramped cells of the child prisoners and fire gas canisters for no reason, causing them to choke and collapse to the floor,” Ghassan added.

Muin is considering dropping out of school because all his friends have moved up to the 11th grade while he remains in the 10th.

His father, who is also his mathematics teacher, explains that his reluctance to continue his education is linked to the pain he still carries, even after regaining his freedom.

In an October 2025 submission to the UN Committee Against Torture, the rights group Defense for Children International-Palestine said 74 percent of 325 Palestinian child detainees whose testimonies it collected reported being subjected to violence.

Of those surveyed, 26 percent said they had been interrogated under duress, while 21 percent reported being held in solitary confinement for two days or more as a means of exerting pressure during interrogation.

Ayed Abu Qtaish, a child rights expert, told Al Jazeera that the psychological stress children endure during detention doesn’t necessarily end on their release; the effects can persist long after they are freed.

He said conditions inside detention facilities prevent children from leading a normal life while in custody, quite apart from the repression inflicted upon Palestinian detainees, including children.

This process leaves detainees in a state of constant state of hyper-vigilance and psychological exhaustion.

“These conditions have contributed to the prevalence of psychological disorders and mental health issues among detainees, and the impact of these experiences is more profound on children due to their young age and psychological vulnerability,” he concluded.

articles.title: Nigella Lawson is 'brilliant addition' to The Great British Bake Off, TV critics say
articles.summary: The TV chef joined Paul Hollywood in the tent as the Channel 4 competition returned for a new series.
articles.body:
TV critics have described Nigella Lawson as the "icing on the cake" of The Great British Bake Off, after the show returned for a new series on Tuesday.

Lawson has replaced Dame Prue Leith, who announced she was leaving earlier this year after nearly a decade in the programme's famous tent.

The Telegraph said Lawson gives the Channel 4 series a "new lease of life", while Digital Spy agreed she was a "brilliant addition" to the line-up.

But the Independent was cooler on the launch episode as a whole, saying the show "wastes Nigella's prodigious charms and misses a chance for a true revamp".

The return of Bake Off saw Lawson join fellow judge Paul Hollywood, who has appeared on the programme since its launch in 2010, and presenters Alison Hammond and Noel Fielding.

Former Bake Off winner Giuseppe Dell'Anno told BBC Radio 4's Today that Lawson "did produce a step change" to the show and was a "nice fit with the ethos of the programme".

"She was doing her best by capturing the vibes of a cake, the feelings, what it makes you think of, which was very nicely balanced by Paul being very technical and scrutinising," he said.

"I think, however, that she will get better over time, because my gut feeling yesterday was that she was still in new territory."

In a five-star review, the Guardian's Lucy Mangan said Lawson "moves through Bake Off dispensing words of wisdom, generous praise and gentle criticism".

She added that Lawson is "just as confident as Leith but a much quieter, more soothing presence that works perfectly with Alison Hammond's ebullience and Paul Hollywood's teacher-ish vibe".

The Telegraph's Anita Singh also awarded five stars, remarking that "Bake Off and Nigella are a match made in heaven".

"She brings glamour, intelligence and poise. And, of course, a hefty dollop of innuendo," Singh said.

"Lawson is supportive in her judging but not afraid to tell the bakers where they can improve. She gives helpful advice."

The launch episode was described as "one of the most disastrous openers ever" by Metro's Adam Miller - but luckily he was only referring to the cakes.

"When Bake Off should be crumbling after 17 seasons, Nigella Lawson is making Channel 4's crown jewel fresher than ever," he said.

"It's clear to see she is the lifeline Bake Off needed to ensure it could easily have another decade or more in it yet."

However, other critics said Channel 4 had missed an opportunity to revitalise the programme.

Awarding two stars, the Independent's Nick Hilton said Lawson quickly "feels part of the fabric".

"But this is also the problem," he continued. "The Bake Off format is very tired. The cakes wobble, the decorations melt, the bakers over-salt the batter, and everything remains the same.

"Nigella's arrival might have been an opportunity for a harder refresh. But instead of bending the format to suit Nigella, the new judge bends to the will of the programme."

Hilton acknowledged that producers "might have done brilliantly to snag Nigella, and it will undoubtedly lead to an uptick in viewers".

"But they've applied her prodigious charms too thinly, and even she – with her preference for all things 'sumptuous' – can't stop the feeling that the show has gone more than a little stale."

Several critics noted that Lawson did not deliver as much innuendo as expected during her debut in the tent.

"Add Nigella – famous for her on-screen coquettish eyelash-fluttering and cheeky language choices – into the mix, and you'd imagine the sauciness gets dialled up to 11," said the Radio Times's Jane Rackham .

"Instead, she's cut back on the sauce. She makes well-informed and helpful comments about the amateur bakers' efforts."

Digital Spy's Janet A Leigh agreed , noting: "As is the nature of Bake Off, there were many opportunities for Nigella to engage with the playful, flirtatious nature that has underpinned the show since its inception. Yet every opportunity was gently rebuffed."

Instead, she said, Lawson "has a way of talking about food that celebrates it and expands the audience's understanding of flavours without seeming pretentious".

"If episode one is just a flavour of what to expect from Nigella, then it is hugely encouraging. She cares deeply, steers wisely, and slots effortlessly into the close-knit team."

When Lawson was faced with innuendo-laden comments from contestants or co-stars, she often "wisely said nothing", noted the Daily Mail's Jan Moir.

"Ultimately this was a tremendous debut performance from the new mistress of meringue, showing a side of Nigella we have not seen before: quirky, commanding, funny – but also humane," she concluded.

Ben Dowell of the Times observed : "Bake Off has always been one of TV's more beguiling offerings with a comforting romance about it.

"It's not perfect. Hammond is ebullience and warmth personified but her co-presenter, the erstwhile Mighty Boosh comedian Fielding, still looks a bit lost, as if he has wandered in from the wrong set.

"But with Nigella the show is definitely in safe hands. Bake Off has found a new star."

articles.title: New Zealand spent 14 years removing pests and weeds from Abel Tasman; the national park now has flourishing native wildlife and restored forest
articles.summary: Rest of World News: The Abel Tasman National Park can still look much as visitors might expect from a New Zealand wilderness: forest, rivers, beaches and a coastline open.
articles.body: The Abel Tasman National Park can still look much as visitors might expect from a New Zealand wilderness: forest, rivers, beaches and a coastline opening onto the sea. Yet beneath that familiar scenery, the park has undergone a long ecological repair. According to the Project Janszoon official website it began in 2012, parts of the park had lost much of their natural richness to introduced predators and invasive plants. Fourteen years of pest control, weed removal, habitat work, species recovery and education have since changed what can be heard and seen across the landscape. Native birds are returning to places where they have become scarce, forest plants are recovering and a wider community has become involved in looking after the park.A 14-year restoration effort began in New Zealand’s Abel TasmanThe Abel Tasman had the appearance of an intact landscape when Project Janszoon was established. Its ecological condition told a less reassuring story. Introduced pests were affecting native wildlife, while weeds were competing with indigenous vegetation. Some of the park's forests had become unusually quiet because birds that once formed part of the everyday soundscape were no longer common in many areas.That became the starting point for Project Janszoon, a conservation partnership launched in 2012 with the Department of Conservation (DOC), mana whenua, the Abel Tasman Birdsong Trust and local communities. Project Janszoon founder Devon said, “It was the first time that philanthropy at scale had really injected funding into one of these projects. What was different was we were able to look at the national park as a whole, whereas DOC had always focused on the pressure points.”According to Project Janszoon, more than $21 million was invested in the restoration work over 14 years.Abel Tasman’s restoration went beyond removing pests and invasive plantsMuch of the restoration has involved work that visitors may not immediately notice. Predator control helped create safer conditions for native birds, while teams and volunteers worked against invasive vegetation. Wilding pines were removed, and gorse and other weeds have been tackled along beaches and elsewhere in the park. The purpose was not simply to clear unwanted plants or reduce pest numbers. The wider aim was to give native species enough space and protection to re-establish themselves.Some of the changes are now visible in the forest. Mistletoe and rata are among the native plants making a return, while areas once affected by invasive vegetation have been brought back towards a more indigenous character.Native birds began appearing againThe clearest signs of change can be found in the wildlife. Kākā have returned to areas of the park, while whio and pāteke have also been recorded. For people who knew the park before the restoration programme, the change is particularly noticeable in the sounds of the bush.Ropata Taylor, chair of the Ngāti Rārua Ātiawa Iwi Trust, described, “You were struck by how quiet and silent the bush was. Now in 2026, it is like a different place. The diversity of plants, the sounds of the manu. It has gone from this kind of quite sterile state to this vibrant living state.”The project reached beyond the forestProject Janszoon's work was not confined to ecological management. More than 10,000 students took part in its youth ambassador and education programmes, giving younger generations direct experience of the park and its restoration work. That educational element became part of a broader change in how the Abel Tasman was cared for. DOC's Martin Rodd said, “The work on the ground, the biodiversity achievements, have been amazing. But the ownership of it, to me that was the magic. We need to keep building on that.”The park's restoration therefore involved people as well as habitats. Volunteers continued weed control, communities participated in conservation activity, and iwi and other partners became part of the longer-term stewardship of the area.The philanthropic partnership behind Abel Tasman’s 14-year restorationProject Janszoon was unusual in New Zealand because of the scale of private funding directed towards a national park. Neal and Annette Plowman supported the project and later established the NEXT Foundation, a philanthropic organisation that has committed $250 million to education and environmental work.For Project Janszoon, philanthropy provided an opportunity to work across the park over a sustained period rather than concentrating only on individual pressure points. The arrangement brought together private funding, conservation expertise, government agencies, iwi and community groups. The model has since been used in other conservation projects around New Zealand.For the Plowmans, the Abel Tasman project became a long-term commitment rather than a short funding exercise. In February 2026, representatives of Ngāti Rārua, Ngāti Tama and Te Ātiawa presented them with a wheku, a carved post, on the coastal track above Rākauroa/Anchorage in recognition of their contribution.The next phase of Abel Tasman’s restoration begins after 14 yearsProject Janszoon's formal role came to an end on 30 June 2026. That does not mark the end of the restoration programme. DOC and the NEXT Foundation have signed what is known as the Tomorrow Accord, under which DOC has committed to maintaining agreed biodiversity gains achieved during the project's 14 years. The responsibility now shifts more firmly towards the Department of Conservation, mana whenua, landowners, communities and other organisations involved in the park. The change is important because ecological recovery can be lost if pest control, weed management and monitoring stop. The progress made in Abel Tasman depends on those gains being maintained over time.Native wildlife and forest plants are returning to Abel TasmanFourteen years ago, the Abel Tasman could appear untouched while carrying many of the ecological pressures common to protected areas affected by introduced species and invasive plants. By 2026, the evidence of restoration is easier to encounter. Kākā move along the coast. Whio and pāteke occupy waterways. Robins are appearing near beaches again. Native forest plants are returning, while invasive vegetation has been pushed back.The most striking change may be less visible than any of these individual species. It is the return of a richer, noisier and more varied forest environment. Project Janszoon has finished its own chapter in the park's history. The next one belongs to the organisations, iwi, volunteers and communities now responsible for keeping those ecological gains in place.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1998, Chicago mother Kimberly Wasserman went door-to-door after her baby’s asthma attack; by 2012, the city’s Fisk and Crawford coal plants had closed
articles.summary: US News: In 1998, Kimberly Wasserman was a young single mother living in Chicago’s Little Village neighbourhood when her three-month-old son suddenly began gas.
articles.body: In 1998, Kimberly Wasserman was a young single mother living in Chicago’s Little Village neighbourhood when her three-month-old son suddenly began gasping for air. She rushed him to hospital, where doctors told her he had suffered an asthma attack. The frightening episode would change the direction of her life. Instead of treating it as an isolated incident, Wasserman began asking what in the air around her home could be affecting her child.According to the Goldman Environmental Prize, Wasserman lived less than a mile from the Crawford Generating Station, one of two coal-fired power plants operating on Chicago’s southwest side. The other was the Fisk Street Generating Station. Their smokestacks stood close to densely populated neighbourhoods, and coal storage and other industrial activity heightened residents’ concerns about air quality. A Harvard study later estimated that emissions from the two plants were associated with more than 40 premature deaths, 550 emergency-room visits and 2,800 asthma attacks each year.From a frightening diagnosis to a neighbourhood campaignAfter her son's asthma attack, Wasserman started collaborating with an environmental justice group called the Little Village Environmental Justice Organisation, which is known as LVEJO for short. She would go door-to-door with her child, talking to other families who were experiencing the same kind of respiratory issues. The protest movement grew gradually rather than from a single event. Residents held meetings, attended hearings and staged protests, while community activists used “Toxic Tours” to draw attention to industrial pollution. Wasserman and other activists also contacted health, labour, religious and environmental organisations.The health concerns were not based only on anecdotal reports. Research examining the Chicago plants later provided evidence of what happened after they shut down. A study published in the American Journal of Public Health analysed asthma-related emergency-department visits among children aged four and under between 2009 and 2017. It found that asthma-related emergency-department visits fell by about 12% in areas near Chicago coal plants after the plants closed, compared with areas farther away.A campaign that reached City HallClosing the power plants seemed impossible for years as both Fisk and Crawford were already among Chicago’s oldest coal plants. They were owned by Midwest Generation, setting up a fight between activists and politicians. Progress came when the Chicago Clean Power Coalition formed in 2011. The coalition lobbied for the passing of the Clean Power Ordinance, which would compel the power plants to adopt stricter pollution controls. As noted by the Goldman Environmental Prize, the ordinance was supported by 35 members of the City Council and Mayor Rahm Emanuel. In response, Midwest Generation decided to shut down both power plants.The closure was announced in February 2012. Crawford and Fisk subsequently closed that year, ahead of previously expected timelines. Illinois Environmental Protection Agency records confirm that Crawford operated from 1924 until 2012, while federal and state agencies monitored the sites during and after their shutdown. Their closure marked the end of coal-fired electricity generation at two long-running Chicago facilities and opened the way for discussions about the future use and redevelopment of the former industrial sites.What happened after the smokestacks stoppedThe closing of these plants was a significant event, but it did not end Little Village’s environmental problems. The old industrial sites continued to draw attention because of redevelopment plans and lingering pollution concerns. For example, the Illinois EPA says Crawford was decommissioned after its 2012 closure, when the coal and coal ash were removed, and the site was acquired for redevelopment.However, Wasserman's contribution went further than just the campaign for closing the plants. According to the Goldman Environmental Prize, she and the community activists advocated that the area occupied by the industrial facilities should become parks and recreational spaces. History of LVEJO mentions how the organisation contributed to the closure of the plants and ensured community benefits for the sites.What began as one mother’s response to her child’s asthma attack grew into a community-wide effort. Wasserman’s story connected a personal health crisis with industrial pollution, public activism and the future of the neighbourhood’s land. By 2012, the two coal plants near Little Village were no longer producing electricity, and later studies found health benefits for children.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
